summary: BBN announces that IMP number 5 will go off the network on the morning of Saturday March 4, 1972 for a move to a new location, and that a new host called BBN-1D will later join for Network Control Center functions.

plainLanguage.summary: A heads-up that a network box will be turned off while it is moved, and a new computer will be added afterward.

subtitle: Scheduled maintenance of the BBN IMP and addition of a new host

tldr.problem: BBN's network equipment needed to be relocated but the operation had to minimize disruption to ARPANET users.
tldr.mechanism: BBN announced a scheduled maintenance window on Saturday morning to move the IMP number 5 to a new location, with a commitment to restore service by the afternoon and to add a new host (BBN-1D) afterward.
tldr.outcome: By scheduling the maintenance on a weekend morning, impact on network users was minimized, and a new host was added to support additional Network Control Center functions.

today: RFC 301 is a routine maintenance notice from the earliest days of ARPANET. It illustrates how even small infrastructure changes required network-wide coordination and planning to avoid disrupting research activities across dozens of institutions.

sections.title: IMP 5 Maintenance Schedule
sections.content: BBN announced that on Saturday morning, March 4, 1972, at 8:00 AM EST, their IMP number 5 would go off the network to allow relocation of the equipment to a new facility within BBN. The Network Control Center telephone and operators would remain available during this period. The team aimed to restore the IMP to the network by early Saturday afternoon.
sections.plainLanguage: One of the network boxes will be turned off Saturday morning so it can be moved to a new room in the building.

sections.title: Minimizing Impact
sections.content: The choice of Saturday morning was made intentionally to minimize network impact. If unexpected delays caused the lines to stay down longer than anticipated, the effect on other sites would be reduced compared to a weekday outage. All other sites were expected to operate normally during this period, with only BBN IMP number 5 offline.
sections.plainLanguage: They picked Saturday morning so that if something goes wrong, fewer people working on the network will be affected.

sections.title: Adding a New Host
sections.content: Shortly after the move, BBN would connect a new host to the network: a PDP-1D minicomputer that would assist with Network Control Center functions. The host would be named BBN-1D and would have network address 197. It would not function as a server site but would provide additional computational resources for NCC operations.
sections.plainLanguage: After the move is done, a new computer called BBN-1D will be connected to help run the network control office.

references.text: Alter, R., "BBN IMP (#5) and NCC Schedule March 4, 1971", RFC 301, February 1972.
